mentions.story: Ask HN: Which online courses and books can provide real value to a programmer?
mentions.text:
There is a 3 part course on Coursera by U of Washington Prof Dan Grossman called

Programming Languages A: [course]

Programming Languages B: [course]

Programming Languages C: [course]

It will surely make you a great programmer if you haven't dabbled with functional languages before. Even if you have, it still makes a great course only for the teaching style of Dan.

mentions.story: A Lisp interpreter written in Lisp (2017)
mentions.text: I recently completed Programming languages - Part B, by Dan Grossman on coursera ( [course]). The homework in Racket was a very similar problem. Needless to say it was mindbending and to get the final interpreter work with all those expressions(nested) / lambdas was so satisfying!

mentions.author: schot
mentions.text:
The Coursera course Programming Languages (Part A and B) by Dan Grossman teaches FP (and more) using SML and Racket. I enjoyed this course a lot. I would not recommend it for kids, but it should be great for students with some limited programming experience.

mentions.author: nikofeyn
mentions.text:
as others have said, the little schemer (for functions) and also the little mler (for types) are purpose built to thinking about functions and types recursively.

also, the coursera course programming languages by dan grossman is an excellent course on doing things recursively. in part a, you learn sml, and in part b, you learn racket and build a simple interpreter.
